question: Can a steeper actual front supply a different outer-highlight normal distribution while an optically derived positive back retains the existing physical source-plane correspondence?
motivating_evidence: Current working front is half the positive spline. Its highlight is too broad and the cap/outer rim differ. Material-basis corrections cannot repair those structures. One fixed steeper front tests actual surface-normal distribution, not added light or a warp.
initialization: The selected flat-front geometric map is a diagnostic design target, not photographic truth. No target image or source RGB is read.
unknown: One real radial back-height profile B, common to both lengths. Surface is reconstructed from optical boundary equations; no image displacement correction after tracing.
method: One backward ODE construction with front equal to the canonical positive spline, retaining n1.5/D2.1 and the same physical correspondence prior used in17. Require positive single-valued actual Hermite back and global bounds; no RGB or native grid.
checkpoint: Same-surface Snell equation sign, positive solve interval and finite budget before integration; positive/singlevalued endpoint and global profile bounds before any future forward render.
stop: One fixed front_scale1 construction, first invariant/branch/positivity failure or deadline. No alternate scale, profile smoothing, source/mask change or native rendering. A valid construction only enables a separately bounded forward/source experiment.
ownership: Root private experiment only, shared old tracer untouched during this design. Existing helper continues separate Search work through Sessionsation.
